taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Claude-formatted title and authors did not match the real linked article, yet the inaccurate citation entered a court-facing expert declaration; the artefact therefore did not meet the source-fidelity threshold required for formal legal reliance.

The May 23 court order identifies a specific standing-order requirement for lead trial counsel to certify personal verification of content accuracy and expressly states that neither the certification nor verification had occurred before filing.

Claude’s formatted citation attributed the real article to the wrong authors and title while retaining the correct journal and URL, making the source identity materially false in the filed declaration.

Counsel corrected volume and pages yet missed false authors and title, illuminating the gap between partial metadata checks and full citation accuracy; the record does not establish that the partial check was itself represented as final verification.
